raw_case_text:
A 70-year-old male with a past medical history of low testosterone, hypertension, benign prostatic hyperplasia, and no known travel history presented with confusion and headache in South Carolina. The patient had been recently treated for community-acquired pneumonia and completed a 5-day course of amoxicillin/clavulanic acid as an outpatient. He presented 5 days later after developing a frontal headache and short-term memory deficits. Vital signs were significant for a fever of 100.4. Physical exam revealed lethargy without any focal neurological deficits. A CT scan of the head was normal. Lumbar puncture showed a cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) WBC of 103 K/mm3 with a differential of 55% lymphocytes, 7% neutrophils, 8% monocytes, glucose 56 mg/dL, and protein 180 mg/dL. Opening pressure was 15 cm H2O. The patient was started on vancomycin, ceftriaxone, ampicillin, and acyclovir for empiric treatment of meningitis and encephalitis. CSF studies were negative for cryptococcal antigen, Lyme IgM antibody, Toxoplasmosis IgG antibody, varicella, VDRL, and CMV. Viral HSV PCR was pending and bacterial gram stain, culture, and fungal culture revealed no growth on day 3 of hospitalization. The patient rapidly improved and was discharged with suspected viral meningitis on acyclovir.
The patient returned to the hospital one day after discharge with new onset right-sided weakness and dysarthria. MRI of the brain revealed T2/flair signal abnormalities in the left frontal lobe with associated parenchymal enhancement (refer to Figure 1). Repeat LP was performed and CSF showed a WBC of 621 mg/dL with a differential of 85% lymphocyte, 29% PMNs, 16% monocytes, CSF glucose 21 mg/dL, and CSF protein 127 mg/dL. Opening pressure was 19 cm H2O. CSF fungal cultures from the previous admission grew Cryptococcus gattii after 5 days. HIV and hepatitis B and C were negative; serum IgA, IgM, and IgG levels and ANA were normal. Repeat CSF antigen was obtained but not resulted, and gram stain and bacterial cultures showed no growth. Fungal cultures grew C. gattii in 3 days. The patient was started on induction therapy of IV liposomal Amphotericin and Fluconazole for four weeks. A third LP was performed after two weeks of induction therapy with LFA-confirmed positive cryptococcal antigen and a titer of 1 : 2560 on LA. There was no growth on fungal culture. Repeat weekly LPs showed decreasing CSF antigen to 1 : 80 titers and continued sterile fungal cultures. The patient was transitioned and discharged on oral Fluconazole for maintenance therapy. Ten days later, the patient returned to the hospital after suffering a large brainstem lacunar stroke (refer to Figure 2). He was transitioned to inpatient hospice and later expired.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 70-year-old male in South Carolina presented with fever, frontal headache, confusion, and short-term memory deficits 5 days after completing amoxicillin/clavulanic acid for community-acquired pneumonia, and returned 1 day after discharge with acute right-sided weakness and dysarthria.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Five days after completing a 5-day outpatient course of amoxicillin/clavulanic acid for community-acquired pneumonia, the patient presented with fever (100.4 °F), frontal headache, lethargy, and short-term memory deficits. Discharged on oral acyclovir after rapid clinical improvement and negative day 3 preliminary bacterial/fungal cultures, he returned 1 day later with acute right-sided hemiparesis and dysarthria, and 10 days after completing subsequent 4-week inpatient antifungal induction therapy re-presented with a large brainstem stroke.
subjective.past_medical_history: Hypertension, benign prostatic hyperplasia, low testosterone, and recent community-acquired pneumonia. Social history: resident of South Carolina with no known travel history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Initial presentation: fever (100.4 °F), frontal headache, lethargy, and short-term memory loss. Readmission (1 day post-discharge): acute right-sided weakness and slurred speech (dysarthria).

objective.physical_examination: Initial admission: temperature 100.4 °F, lethargic without focal neurological deficits. First readmission: new-onset right-sided motor weakness and dysarthria.
objective.routine_investigations: HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C serologies were negative; serum IgA, IgM, IgG levels and ANA were normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial head CT was normal. Initial lumbar puncture showed opening pressure 15 cmH2O, CSF WBC 103/mm3 (55% lymphocytes, 7% neutrophils, 8% monocytes), glucose 56 mg/dL, protein 180 mg/dL, and negative initial cryptococcal antigen, Lyme IgM, Toxoplasma IgG, VZV, VDRL, cytomegalovirus (CMV), HSV PCR, and Gram stain; however, the admission CSF fungal culture grew Cryptococcus gattii after 5 days. Readmission brain MRI revealed left frontal lobe T2/FLAIR hyperintensity with parenchymal enhancement, and repeat LP showed opening pressure 19 cmH2O, CSF WBC 621/mm3 (85% lymphocytes, 29% PMNs, 16% monocytes), glucose 21 mg/dL, protein 127 mg/dL, and repeat CSF fungal culture growing C. gattii in 3 days (week 2 LP confirmed positive CSF cryptococcal antigen by LFA with latex agglutination titer 1:2,560, declining to 1:80 on weekly LPs with sterile cultures). Second readmission neuroimaging demonstrated a large brainstem lacunar stroke.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis of Cryptococcus gattii meningoencephalitis in an HIV-negative, immunocompetent host in South Carolina (confirmed by growth of C. gattii from two sequential CSF fungal cultures and a CSF cryptococcal antigen titer of 1:2,560, after initial false-negative CSF CrAg; CMV, VZV, HSV, Lyme, Toxoplasma, and neurosyphilis ruled out), complicated by left frontal parenchymal involvement and a fatal late brainstem lacunar stroke. Treated with a 4-week induction course of intravenous liposomal amphotericin B plus fluconazole (achieving sterile CSF cultures and CrAg titer reduction from 1:2,560 to 1:80) and discharged on oral fluconazole maintenance; 10 days post-discharge, he suffered a large brainstem lacunar infarction, was transitioned to inpatient hospice, and died.
